correctness.rationale: Every parameter case is exhausted. For r>=2, the least prime a>r and delta=a-r give an immediate witness when delta=1. For delta>=2, an exact positive-coefficient identity proves U=r+p(p-r)/delta>7L/5 with L=p^2/a. The published consecutive-prime ratio lemma then gives q<=U outside three named transitions; only 7->11 can occur, reducing to two explicit small witnesses. The r=1 and p<=r cases are complete, and an exact checker corroborates the finite prime-ratio computation and witness construction.

value.rationale: The result resolves an explicit conjecture in the foundational paper on sparse Schemmel totients. It upgrades bounded verification to a uniform proof for all positive r and all primes p, using a structural witness from the least admissible prime and a controlled next prime. This is a global classification of the prime-square layer, not a routine finite increment.
